title: Observability experiment matrix for feature flags
content:
Purpose:

This is a working plan for how we will instrument, monitor, and visualize short-lived feature experiments (feature flags, canaries, dark launches) across the inference stack. The intent: make experimentation low-friction for product/ML teams while keeping operation risk low and query/ingest cost predictable.

Context / constraints:
- Many experiments are transient (hours → weeks), but generate high-cardinality telemetry if left unbounded.
- Primary consumers: product experiment owners, model owners, SRE on-call.
- Cost sensitivity: long retention / high-cardinality dashboards are expensive; prefer ephemeral views and sampling.
- We must avoid duplicate instrumentation across infra and product teams. Use canonical metric names and tag schema.

High-level goals (measurable):
- Fast visibility: baseline vs experiment within 10 minutes of rollout for traffic > 1rps.
- Low noise: limit per-experiment cardinality to 3 tags of high-cardinality (flag_id, cohort, region) + bounded value sets.
- Cost guardrails: estimate & cap query ingestion from experiments to < 6% of daily metric cost baseline.
- Safety: automated rollback signal(s) for latency regressions and error-rate spikes.

Experiment types covered:
1) Model variant swap (A/B model weights).
2) Prompt augmentation or pre/post-processing change.
3) Routing policy change (region/cost-tier steering).
4) Feature-level flag that enables new downstream post-processing (e.g., reranker).

Metric tiers (naming convention: experiment.<flag>.<metric>):
- Primary (must be computed for every experiment):
  - experiment.<flag>.success_rate: percent successful responses (status==200 && !semantic_error)
  - experiment.<flag>.p50_lat_ms, p95_lat_ms, p99_lat_ms: inference latency quantiles (end-to-end)
  - experiment.<flag>.token_rate: tokens/sec consumed by experiment traffic
- Secondary (computed at lower resolution / sampled):
  - experiment.<flag>.cost_per_token_estimate: rolling average cost estimate derived from resource-tags
  - experiment.<flag>.output_quality: discrete eval proxy (synthetic eval pass rate or small eval set match)
- Diagnostic (high-cardinality, sampled):
  - experiment.<flag>.model_trace_spans: span-level events collected for a small percent of requests
  - experiment.<flag>.kv_hits: prefix/KV cache hit rate for experiment cohort

Tagging and cardinality rules:
- Reserved tags: flag_id, experiment_cohort, model_version, region, customer_tier
- Cardinality limits: flag_id (unbounded number across org) — to be sharded into ephemeral views; experiment_cohort limited to {control,variant1,variant2} for dashboarding; model_version should be canonical short name (no commit hashes)
- Avoid using free-text prompt or user-provided ids in metric tags. Use hashed identifiers only when necessary and with sample-based collection.

Tracing strategy:
- Full traces not kept for all experiment traffic. Use adaptive sampling:
  - baseline: 0.5% trace sampling for experiment traffic
  - elevated: 5% when p95_lat or error_rate crosses thresholds (see alerts)
  - targeted: retain full traces for up to 1000 requests post-rollout to investigate first regressions
- Trace attributes to include: trace_experiment=flag_id, cohort, model_version, seq_len_bucket, kv_cache_used (bool), route_path
- If experiment touches private deployments, redact PII/PHI per privacy checklist before including in traces

Dashboard templates and ephemeral views:
- Each experiment gets a lightweight ephemeral dashboard (ttl=14 days) created from a template. Template panels:
  1) Traffic and cohort split (bar + sparkline)
  2) Latency quantiles (p50/p95/p99) with delta vs baseline
  3) Success rate and error taxonomy (4xx/5xx/semantic errors)
  4) Cost estimate (tokens * model_cost) and unit cost trend
  5) Key spans sampled (link to trace explorer filtered by flag_id)
- Dashboard UI should surface quick actions: increase sampling, pin for retention, export csv, and create rollback runbook.

Alerting heuristic (auto-generated for experiments):
- Latency regressions: if experiment.p95_lat_ms > baseline.p95_lat_ms * 1.35 for 10m AND traffic > 5rps => page SRE
- Error spike: if experiment.success_rate drops by >5 percentage points compared to baseline over 5m with >100 requests => page SRE
- Cost surge: if experiment.cost_estimate daily > 3x expected baseline estimate for 30m => page product-owner (email)
- Flaky output: if output_quality falls below configured threshold (default 80%) for 10m => alert to model-owner channel

Data retention & query cost controls:
- Ephemeral experiment metrics: 14 days high-resolution (1s/10s buckets), then downsample to 1h precision for 90 days, remove high-cardinality indexes at 90 days
- Traces: sampled trace retention 30 days, targeted full-trace retention 90 days for critical incidents with manual approval
- On creation of a new experiment dashboard, estimate: expected qps * 24 * 14 to compute expected increased query cost; if over threshold, require product-owner signoff

Implementation checklist (minimum viable):
- [ ] Instrument experiment flag router to attach flag_id and cohort to request context (correlate with request_id)
- [ ] Emit experiment.* metrics at ingress and end-of-request with standardized tags
- [ ] Hook adaptive tracer sampling rules to experiment flags
- [ ] Add dashboard template and CLI to instantiate ephemeral dashboards with ttl
- [ ] Automate alert generation for experiment (thresholds derived from historical baseline or absolute defaults)

Rollout observability smoke tests (pre-flight):
- Push a tiny traffic blast (1k requests) to variant cohort in staging, confirm:
  - Metrics appear in <2 min
  - Dashboard panels show cohort split correctly
  - Sampled traces are discoverable by tag filter
- Run cost estimate job and verify numbers are within expected bounds

Ownership model:
- Experiment owner (product or ML) responsible for: defining success_metric, expected delta, and cohort sizes in experiment RFC; tagging the experiment in the creation form
- Observability infra: provide templates, enforce tag schema, maintain sampling rules, on-call for metric ingestion issues

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we automatically expire flag_ids after N experiments per month to limit namespace growth? (tradeoff: historical auditability)
- How to best represent multi-flag interactions where combinatorial cohorts explode cardinality? (proposal: limit to pairwise instrumentation and sample combinations)
- Is 14-day ephemeral retention sufficient for longer A/Bs? Provide opt-in pin-to-retain flow in dashboard UI.

Next steps (short horizon):
- Run pilot with 3 internal experiments (PM + ML) in Nov 2025 to validate dashboards and sampling rules
- Build PR with instrumentation helpers (github: observability/pull/412) and an experiment dashboard CLI
- Draft RBAC and retention policy for experiments in compliance channel

Notes to self: keep experiment flag names short and avoid using product-internal acronyms in metric tags. Coordinate with product-telemetry guild to align naming and alert ownership.
